// The inserts of a vector index end to end, through a shard: TestShardE2E
// opens a database as a node opens it, with one class of one shard whose
// vector index is of the type asked for, and imports the train rows of a raw
// dataset as objects, by the call a node serves a batch import with
// (DB.BatchPutObjects). Every object is written to the store of the shard,
// with its vector and its property, and its vector is added to the index,
// inside the clock: what the posting-edge index and HFresh are compared by,
// each paying for the same.
//
// Parameters, from the environment:
//   - PE_DATASET: a raw dataset directory (meta.txt, train.f32 or
//     train.embedded with a train_offset line, test.f32, neighbors.i32).
//   - PE_DIR: where the database goes; it must not exist, or be empty.
//   - PE_OUT: the JSON of the result, written again with every sample of the
//     progress and at every step.
//   - PE_INDEX: "postingedge" or "hfresh". The class has the default user
//     config of the type, with the cosine distance.
//   - PE_CACHE: the rq.cacheMode of the posting-edge index (routing).
//   - PE_CALLERS: how many callers import at once (8).
//   - PE_BATCH: the objects of a batch call (100).
//   - PE_ROWS: the first rows of the dataset that go in (all of them if 0).
//   - PE_SHUFFLE: 0 imports the rows in their order; otherwise they go in
//     the shuffled order of the other harnesses of the index (1).
//   - PE_QUERIES: how many queries are searched afterwards, 0 for none
//     (1000).
//   - PE_PROGRESS: the seconds between two samples of the progress (30).
//   - PE_READERS: how many goroutines read the dataset ahead of the callers
//     (4).
//   - PE_ASYNC: 1 turns async indexing on (0, as a node has it unless
//     ASYNC_INDEXING is set).
//   - PE_IMPORT_FACTOR: the factor of the batch workers of the database,
//     times GOMAXPROCS (1.5, as a node has it).

const shardE2EClass = "ShardE2E"

func shardE2EEnv(name, def string) string {
	if s := os.Getenv(name); s != "" {
		return s
	}
	return def
}

func shardE2EEnvInt(t *testing.T, name string, def int64) int64 {
	s := os.Getenv(name)
	if s == "" {
		return def
	}
	v, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 10, 64)
	require.NoError(t, err, name)
	return v
}

// shardE2EShapes reads the meta.txt of a raw dataset: a line "<name> <a> <b>"
// for each of its files ("train 990000 1536", "test 10000 1536", "neighbors
// 10000 100"), and "train_offset <bytes> 0" when the train vectors are inside
// another file. Any other line is skipped.
func shardE2EShapes(dir string) (map[string][2]int, error) {
	meta, err := os.Open(filepath.Join(dir, "meta.txt"))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer meta.Close()
	shapes := map[string][2]int{}
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(meta)
	for scanner.Scan() {
		fields := strings.Fields(scanner.Text())
		if len(fields) != 3 {
			continue
		}
		a, errA := strconv.Atoi(fields[1])
		b, errB := strconv.Atoi(fields[2])
		if errA == nil && errB == nil {
			shapes[fields[0]] = [2]int{a, b}
		}
	}
	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return shapes, nil
}

// shardE2ETrain is the train set of a raw dataset, read a vector at a time
// from its file: 10M vectors of 768 dimensions are 30.7 GB, more than the run
// should hold.
type shardE2ETrain struct {
	file   *os.File
	offset int64
	rows   int
	dims   int
}

// openShardE2ETrain opens train.f32, or train.embedded when the dataset has
// none: a link to the file the vectors are in, which has them from the byte
// the train_offset line of meta.txt gives.
func openShardE2ETrain(dir string, shapes map[string][2]int) (*shardE2ETrain, error) {
	shape, ok := shapes["train"]
	if !ok || shape[0] <= 0 || shape[1] <= 0 {
		return nil, errors.Errorf("%s: no train line in meta.txt", dir)
	}
	path := filepath.Join(dir, "train.f32")
	if _, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil {
		path = filepath.Join(dir, "train.embedded")
	}
	file, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	train := &shardE2ETrain{file: file, offset: int64(shapes["train_offset"][0]), rows: shape[0], dims: shape[1]}
	info, err := file.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		file.Close()
		return nil, err
	}
	if need := train.offset + 4*int64(train.rows)*int64(train.dims); info.Size() < need {
		file.Close()
		return nil, errors.Errorf("%s has %d bytes, and %d rows of %d dimensions from byte %d take %d",
			path, info.Size(), train.rows, train.dims, train.offset, need)
	}
	return train, nil
}

// read reads the vectors of rows, each into a slice of its own, reusing buf.
func (tr *shardE2ETrain) read(rows []uint32, buf []byte) ([][]float32, []byte, error) {
	size := 4 * tr.dims
	if cap(buf) < size {
		buf = make([]byte, size)
	}
	buf = buf[:size]
	vectors := make([][]float32, len(rows))
	for i, row := range rows {
		if _, err := tr.file.ReadAt(buf, tr.offset+int64(row)*int64(size)); err != nil {
			return nil, buf, errors.Wrapf(err, "read train row %d", row)
		}
		vec := make([]float32, tr.dims)
		byteops.CopyBytesToSlice(vec, buf)
		vectors[i] = vec
	}
	return vectors, buf, nil
}

// shardE2EReadHead reads the first size bytes of a file.
func shardE2EReadHead(path string, size int) ([]byte, error) {
	file, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer file.Close()
	raw := make([]byte, size)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(file, raw); err != nil {
		return nil, errors.Wrapf(err, "read the first %d bytes of %s", size, path)
	}
	return raw, nil
}

// shardE2EReadQueries reads the first limit queries of a raw dataset and, for
// each, the first k of the neighbors it ships: rows of the train set. The
// queries are given to the search as they are stored.
func shardE2EReadQueries(dir string, shapes map[string][2]int, dims, limit, k int) ([][]float32, [][]uint32, error) {
	test, neighbors := shapes["test"], shapes["neighbors"]
	switch {
	case test[0] <= 0:
		return nil, nil, errors.Errorf("%s: no test line in meta.txt", dir)
	case test[1] != dims:
		return nil, nil, errors.Errorf("%s: the queries have %d dimensions, the train rows %d", dir, test[1], dims)
	case neighbors[0] != test[0]:
		return nil, nil, errors.Errorf("%s: %d rows of neighbors for %d queries", dir, neighbors[0], test[0])
	case neighbors[1] < k:
		return nil, nil, errors.Errorf("%s: the dataset ships %d neighbors a query, fewer than %d", dir, neighbors[1], k)
	}
	count := min(limit, test[0])

	raw, err := shardE2EReadHead(filepath.Join(dir, "test.f32"), 4*count*dims)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, err
	}
	queries := make([][]float32, count)
	for q := range queries {
		vec := make([]float32, dims)
		byteops.CopyBytesToSlice(vec, raw[4*q*dims:4*(q+1)*dims])
		queries[q] = vec
	}

	width := neighbors[1]
	raw, err = shardE2EReadHead(filepath.Join(dir, "neighbors.i32"), 4*count*width)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, err
	}
	truth := make([][]uint32, count)
	for q := range truth {
		truth[q] = make([]uint32, k)
		for i := range truth[q] {
			truth[q][i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(raw[4*(q*width+i):])
		}
	}
	return queries, truth, nil
}

// shardE2EUUID is the id of the object of a train row. Its first four bytes
// are the row with its bits reversed, so that the ids are spread over the
// keys of the store as random ones are, whatever the order the rows go in;
// its last four are the row, which a result is read back to. The version and
// the variant are those of a random id.
func shardE2EUUID(row uint32) strfmt.UUID {
	var id uuid.UUID
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(id[0:4], bits.Reverse32(row))
	id[6] = 0x40
	id[8] = 0x80
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(id[12:16], row)
	return strfmt.UUID(id.String())
}

// shardE2ERow is the train row of the object with the id.
func shardE2ERow(id strfmt.UUID) (uint32, error) {
	parsed, err := uuid.Parse(string(id))
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint32(parsed[12:16]), nil
}

// shardE2ERusage is what the system accounts to this process: its time on
// the CPU (getrusage), and the bytes it read from and wrote to disk, its
// page-ins and its footprint (proc_pid_rusage, RUSAGE_INFO_V2).
type shardE2ERusage struct {
	UserSeconds   float64 `json:"userSeconds"`
	SystemSeconds float64 `json:"systemSeconds"`
	CPUSeconds    float64 `json:"cpuSeconds"`
	BytesRead     uint64  `json:"diskBytesRead"`
	BytesWritten  uint64  `json:"diskBytesWritten"`
	Pageins       uint64  `json:"pageins"`
	// Footprint is the footprint when it was read, not an amount since.
	Footprint uint64 `json:"physFootprint"`
}

func readShardE2ERusage() (shardE2ERusage, error) {
	var usage syscall.Rusage
	if err := syscall.Getrusage(syscall.RUSAGE_SELF, &usage); err != nil {
		return shardE2ERusage{}, errors.Wrap(err, "getrusage")
	}
	const procInfoCallPidRusage, rusageInfoV2 = 9, 2
	var buf [256]byte
	_, _, errno := syscall.Syscall6(syscall.SYS_PROC_INFO, procInfoCallPidRusage, uintptr(os.Getpid()), rusageInfoV2, 0,
		uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&buf[0])), 0)
	if errno != 0 {
		return shardE2ERusage{}, errors.Wrap(errno, "read the resource usage of the process")
	}
	// The uint64 of index i of rusage_info_v2, after its uuid of 16 bytes.
	word := func(i int) uint64 { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[16+8*i:]) }
	user, system := time.Duration(usage.Utime.Nano()), time.Duration(usage.Stime.Nano())
	return shardE2ERusage{
		UserSeconds: user.Seconds(), SystemSeconds: system.Seconds(), CPUSeconds: (user + system).Seconds(),
		Pageins: word(4), Footprint: word(7), BytesRead: word(16), BytesWritten: word(17),
	}, nil
}

// since returns what the process was accounted since start was read. The
// footprint stays the one of now.
func (r shardE2ERusage) since(start shardE2ERusage) shardE2ERusage {
	r.UserSeconds -= start.UserSeconds
	r.SystemSeconds -= start.SystemSeconds
	r.CPUSeconds -= start.CPUSeconds
	r.BytesRead -= start.BytesRead
	r.BytesWritten -= start.BytesWritten
	r.Pageins -= start.Pageins
	return r
}

// shardE2EDirBytes sums the sizes of the files under dir.
func shardE2EDirBytes(dir string) (int64, error) {
	var total int64
	err := filepath.WalkDir(dir, func(_ string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
				return nil
			}
			return err
		}
		if d.IsDir() {
			return nil
		}
		info, err := d.Info()
		if err != nil {
			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
				return nil
			}
			return err
		}
		total += info.Size()
		return nil
	})
	return total, err
}

// shardE2EHFreshQueues are the background queues of an HFresh index: its
// analyzes, its splits, its reassignments and its merges. The index keeps
// them to itself (HFresh.taskQueue), and what waits for them is a helper of
// its own tests (waitForMaintenance), so they are reached here by their
// names.
type shardE2EHFreshQueues struct {
	names  []string
	queues []*queue.DiskQueue
}

func shardE2EQueuesOf(index *hfresh.HFresh) (*shardE2EHFreshQueues, error) {
	taskQueue := reflect.ValueOf(index).Elem().FieldByName("taskQueue")
	if !taskQueue.IsValid() || taskQueue.Kind() != reflect.Struct {
		return nil, errors.New("HFresh has no field taskQueue that is a struct")
	}
	diskQueue := func(name string, field reflect.Value) (*queue.DiskQueue, error) {
		if !field.IsValid() || !field.CanAddr() {
			return nil, errors.Errorf("HFresh.taskQueue has no field %s", name)
		}
		found, ok := reflect.NewAt(field.Type(), unsafe.Pointer(field.UnsafeAddr())).Elem().Interface().(*queue.DiskQueue)
		if !ok || found == nil {
			return nil, errors.Errorf("HFresh.taskQueue.%s is a %s, or nil", name, field.Type())
		}
		return found, nil
	}
	out := &shardE2EHFreshQueues{}
	// The queue of the analyzes wraps its disk queue.
	analyze := taskQueue.FieldByName("analyzeQueue")
	if !analyze.IsValid() || analyze.Kind() != reflect.Pointer || analyze.IsNil() {
		return nil, errors.New("HFresh.taskQueue has no analyzeQueue")
	}
	found, err := diskQueue("analyzeQueue.DiskQueue", analyze.Elem().FieldByName("DiskQueue"))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	out.names, out.queues = append(out.names, "analyze"), append(out.queues, found)
	for _, name := range []string{"split", "reassign", "merge"} {
		found, err := diskQueue(name+"Queue", taskQueue.FieldByName(name+"Queue"))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		out.names, out.queues = append(out.names, name), append(out.queues, found)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// pending returns what waits in every queue.
func (q *shardE2EHFreshQueues) pending() map[string]int64 {
	out := make(map[string]int64, len(q.queues))
	for i, dq := range q.queues {
		out[q.names[i]] = dq.Size()
	}
	return out
}

func (q *shardE2EHFreshQueues) size() int64 {
	var total int64
	for _, dq := range q.queues {
		total += dq.Size()
	}
	return total
}

// wait returns once the queues are empty and none of their tasks runs, by
// the calls of the helper of the tests of HFresh (waitForMaintenance): the
// queues are flushed, the scheduler is asked to schedule them now, each is
// waited for, and they are done when nothing is left in them. Apart from
// that helper, the queues must be found empty twice in a row, since a task
// of one puts tasks in another, and a round that finds work sleeps a
// millisecond before the next. Whoever calls it has stopped writing.
func (q *shardE2EHFreshQueues) wait(ctx context.Context) error {
	quiet := 0
	for {
		for i, dq := range q.queues {
			if err := dq.Flush(); err != nil {
				return errors.Wrapf(err, "flush the %s queue", q.names[i])
			}
		}
		q.queues[0].Scheduler().Schedule(ctx)
		for i, dq := range q.queues {
			if err := dq.Wait(ctx); err != nil {
				return errors.Wrapf(err, "wait for the %s queue", q.names[i])
			}
		}
		if q.size() > 0 {
			quiet = 0
			time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
			continue
		}
		quiet++
		if quiet == 2 {
			return nil
		}
	}
}

// shardE2ESample is a sample of the progress: the seconds since the first
// batch call, the objects whose batch call has returned, and how many went in
// a second since the sample before.
type shardE2ESample struct {
	Seconds   float64 `json:"seconds"`
	Inserted  int64   `json:"inserted"`
	PerSecond float64 `json:"perSecond"`
	// Pending is what waits in every background queue of an HFresh index.
	Pending map[string]int64 `json:"pending,omitempty"`
}

// shardE2EPoint is the run at one of its clocks: the seconds since the first
// batch call, the objects of the run over them, and what the system accounted
// to the process meanwhile.
type shardE2EPoint struct {
	Seconds          float64        `json:"seconds"`
	ObjectsPerSecond float64        `json:"objectsPerSecond"`
	Usage            shardE2ERusage `json:"usage"`
}

type shardE2ESearch struct {
	Queries int `json:"queries"`
	K       int `json:"k"`
	// Recall is against the neighbors the dataset ships, which are over every
	// train row: it is left out when not all of them went in.
	Recall *float64 `json:"recall,omitempty"`
	MeanMs float64  `json:"meanMs"`
	P50Ms  float64  `json:"p50Ms"`
	P95Ms  float64  `json:"p95Ms"`
	P99Ms  float64  `json:"p99Ms"`
	MaxMs  float64  `json:"maxMs"`
	QPS    float64  `json:"qps"`
}

type shardE2EResult struct {
	Index string `json:"index"`
	// Config is the user config of the vector index of the class.
	Config    any    `json:"config"`
	Dataset   string `json:"dataset"`
	Dir       string `json:"dir"`
	Rows      int    `json:"rows"`
	TrainRows int    `json:"trainRows"`
	Dims      int    `json:"dims"`
	Shuffled  bool   `json:"shuffled"`
	Callers   int    `json:"callers"`
	BatchSize int    `json:"batchSize"`
	Readers   int    `json:"datasetReaders"`
	Procs     int    `json:"gomaxprocs"`
	// ImportWorkers is the batch workers of the database, which add the
	// vectors of every batch to the index, one each, when async indexing is
	// off. BackgroundWorkers is the workers of the scheduler of the database:
	// the background queues of HFresh, and the queue of the shard when async
	// indexing is on.
	ImportFactor      float64 `json:"importGoroutinesFactor"`
	ImportWorkers     int     `json:"importWorkers"`
	BackgroundWorkers int     `json:"backgroundWorkers"`
	AsyncIndexing     bool    `json:"asyncIndexing"`
	Pid               int     `json:"pid"`

	Inserted int64 `json:"inserted"`
	// LastBatch is the return of the last batch call. BackgroundDone is the
	// vector index with no background work left, and what it writes handed to
	// the system. Flushed is that with every memtable of the shard flushed to
	// a segment besides.
	LastBatch      *shardE2EPoint `json:"lastBatch,omitempty"`
	BackgroundDone *shardE2EPoint `json:"backgroundDone,omitempty"`
	Flushed        *shardE2EPoint `json:"flushed,omitempty"`
	// PendingAtLastBatch is what waited in the background queues of HFresh
	// when the last batch call returned.
	PendingAtLastBatch map[string]int64 `json:"pendingAtLastBatch,omitempty"`
	// DatasetReadSeconds adds up what the readers took to read the rows, ahead
	// of the callers, and CallersFoundNoBatch how many times a caller found
	// no batch read: once a caller at the end, and otherwise the readers did
	// not keep up and the callers waited for the dataset.
	DatasetReadSeconds  float64 `json:"datasetReadSeconds"`
	CallersFoundNoBatch int64   `json:"callersFoundNoBatch"`

	// The heap after two collections, and the files under PE_DIR, both at
	// Flushed: of the whole database, the store of the objects included.
	HeapInuse uint64 `json:"heapInuse"`
	HeapAlloc uint64 `json:"heapAlloc"`
	HeapSys   uint64 `json:"heapSys"`
	Sys       uint64 `json:"sys"`
	DirBytes  int64  `json:"dirBytes"`

	Progress []shardE2ESample `json:"progress"`

	Search *shardE2ESearch `json:"search,omitempty"`
	// PendingAfterSearch is what the searches left in the background queues
	// of HFresh.
	PendingAfterSearch map[string]int64 `json:"pendingAfterSearch,omitempty"`

	ShutdownSeconds float64 `json:"shutdownSeconds"`
	DirBytesAtEnd   int64   `json:"dirBytesAtEnd"`
	Done            bool    `json:"done"`
}

// TestShardE2E imports the dataset through a shard and tells how long it
// took: to the return of the last batch call, and to the vector index with no
// background work left and everything flushed. It then searches the queries
// of the dataset through the database, one at a time.
//
// The database is the one the tests of the package open (openTestDatabase),
// with the settings a node has by default where the tests have others: the
// memtables, the segments, the cycles, the batch workers, the limit of the
// commit logs. The scheduler, the cycles of flush and compaction and the
// cycles of the vector indexes are those of a node, since the database starts
// them.
func TestShardE2E(t *testing.T) {
	datasetDir, dir, out, indexType := os.Getenv("PE_DATASET"), os.Getenv("PE_DIR"), os.Getenv("PE_OUT"), os.Getenv("PE_INDEX")
	if datasetDir == "" || dir == "" || out == "" || indexType == "" {
		t.Skip("no PE_DATASET, PE_DIR, PE_OUT and PE_INDEX given")
	}
	const k = 10
	ctx := context.Background()
	callers := int(shardE2EEnvInt(t, "PE_CALLERS", 8))
	batchSize := int(shardE2EEnvInt(t, "PE_BATCH", 100))
	readers := int(shardE2EEnvInt(t, "PE_READERS", 4))
	queryLimit := int(shardE2EEnvInt(t, "PE_QUERIES", 1000))
	every := time.Duration(shardE2EEnvInt(t, "PE_PROGRESS", 30)) * time.Second
	async := shardE2EEnvInt(t, "PE_ASYNC", 0) != 0
	shuffle := shardE2EEnvInt(t, "PE_SHUFFLE", 1) != 0
	importFactor := config.DefaultMaxImportGoroutinesFactor
	if s := os.Getenv("PE_IMPORT_FACTOR"); s != "" {
		v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64)
		require.NoError(t, err, "PE_IMPORT_FACTOR")
		importFactor = v
	}
	require.Positive(t, callers, "PE_CALLERS")
	require.Positive(t, batchSize, "PE_BATCH")
	require.Positive(t, readers, "PE_READERS")
	require.Positive(t, int64(every), "PE_PROGRESS")
	require.Positive(t, importFactor, "PE_IMPORT_FACTOR")

	shapes, err := shardE2EShapes(datasetDir)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	train, err := openShardE2ETrain(datasetDir, shapes)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer train.file.Close()
	n := train.rows
	if rows := int(shardE2EEnvInt(t, "PE_ROWS", 0)); rows > 0 {
		n = min(n, rows)
	}

	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755))
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Empty(t, entries, "%s is not empty", dir)

	// The default user config of the type, with the cosine distance.
	var userConfig any
	switch indexType {
	case vectorindex.VectorIndexTypePostingEdge:
		uc := postingedgeent.NewDefaultUserConfig()
		uc.Distance = vectorIndexCommon.DistanceCosine
		uc.RQ.CacheMode = shardE2EEnv("PE_CACHE", postingedgeent.CacheModeRouting)
		require.NoError(t, uc.Validate())
		userConfig = uc
	case vectorindex.VectorIndexTypeHFresh:
		uc := hfreshent.NewDefaultUserConfig()
		uc.Distance = vectorIndexCommon.DistanceCosine
		userConfig = uc
	default:
		t.Fatalf("PE_INDEX is %q: it is %q or %q", indexType, vectorindex.VectorIndexTypePostingEdge,
			vectorindex.VectorIndexTypeHFresh)
	}
	class := &models.Class{
		Class:             shardE2EClass,
		VectorIndexType:   indexType,
		VectorIndexConfig: userConfig,
		// As the tests of the package have it (invertedConfig), without the
		// indexes of the null state and of the property lengths, which a class
		// does not have unless it asks for them.
		InvertedIndexConfig: &models.InvertedIndexConfig{
			CleanupIntervalSeconds: 60,
			Stopwords:              &models.StopwordConfig{Preset: "none"},
			UsingBlockMaxWAND:      config.DefaultUsingBlockMaxWAND,
		},
		Properties: []*models.Property{{Name: "row", DataType: schema.DataTypeInt.PropString()}},
	}

	logger := logrus.New()
	logger.SetLevel(logrus.WarnLevel)
	eager := false
	repo := openTestDatabase(t, dir, singleShardState(), monitoring.GetMetrics(), func(c *Config) {
		// The shard is opened at once, for its vector index to be reached.
		c.EnableLazyLoadShards = &eager
		c.AsyncIndexingEnabled = async
		// What a node has by default (configure_api.go and the defaults of
		// usecases/config), where the tests of the package have zero or
		// something else.
		c.TrackVectorDimensions = false
		c.MaxImportGoroutinesFactor = importFactor
		c.MemtablesFlushDirtyAfter = config.DefaultPersistenceMemtablesFlushDirtyAfter
		c.MemtablesInitialSizeMB = 10
		c.MemtablesMaxSizeMB = config.DefaultPersistenceMemtablesMaxSize
		c.MemtablesMinActiveSeconds = config.DefaultPersistenceMemtablesMinDuration
		c.MemtablesMaxActiveSeconds = config.DefaultPersistenceMemtablesMaxDuration
		c.MinMMapSize = config.DefaultPersistenceMinMMapSize
		c.MaxReuseWalSize = config.DefaultPersistenceMaxReuseWalSize
		c.SegmentInfoIntoFileNameEnabled = true
		c.MaxSegmentSize = config.DefaultPersistenceLSMMaxSegmentSize
		c.CycleManagerRoutinesFactor = config.DefaultPersistenceLSMCycleManagerRoutinesFactor
		c.HNSWMaxLogSize = config.DefaultPersistenceHNSWMaxLogSize
		c.HNSWFlatSearchConcurrency = config.DefaultHNSWFlatSearchConcurrency
		c.HNSWAcornFilterRatio = config.DefaultHNSWAcornFilterRatio
		c.VisitedListPoolMaxSize = config.DefaultHNSWVisitedListPoolSize
	}, nil, class)
	closed := false
	defer func() {
		if closed {
			return
		}
		if err := repo.Shutdown(context.Background()); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("shut the database down: %v", err)
		}
	}()

	// The shard of the class, its vector index and the queue of its vectors.
	classIndex := repo.GetIndex(shardE2EClass)
	require.NotNil(t, classIndex)
	var shard *Shard
	require.NoError(t, classIndex.ForEachShard(func(_ string, s ShardLike) error {
		loaded, ok := s.(*Shard)
		if !ok {
			return errors.Errorf("a shard of %T: the test opens its shards at once", s)
		}
		shard = loaded
		return nil
	}))
	require.NotNil(t, shard)
	var pe *postingedge.Persistent
	var hf *hfresh.HFresh
	require.NoError(t, shard.ForEachVectorIndex(func(_ string, vectorIndex VectorIndex) error {
		switch found := vectorIndex.(type) {
		case *postingedge.Persistent:
			pe = found
		case *hfresh.HFresh:
			hf = found
		default:
			return errors.Errorf("the vector index of the class is a %T", vectorIndex)
		}
		return nil
	}))
	var vq *VectorIndexQueue
	require.NoError(t, shard.ForEachVectorQueue(func(_ string, found *VectorIndexQueue) error {
		vq = found
		return nil
	}))
	require.NotNil(t, vq)
	var queues *shardE2EHFreshQueues
	switch indexType {
	case vectorindex.VectorIndexTypePostingEdge:
		require.NotNil(t, pe, "the vector index of the class is not a posting-edge index")
	case vectorindex.VectorIndexTypeHFresh:
		require.NotNil(t, hf, "the vector index of the class is not an HFresh index")
		// Before anything is imported: a run does not get to its end to find
		// that the queues are not where they were.
		queues, err = shardE2EQueuesOf(hf)
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}

	result := &shardE2EResult{
		Index: indexType, Config: userConfig, Dataset: datasetDir, Dir: dir, Rows: n, TrainRows: train.rows,
		Dims: train.dims, Shuffled: shuffle, Callers: callers, BatchSize: batchSize, Readers: readers,
		Procs: runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0), ImportFactor: importFactor,
		ImportWorkers:     int(math.Round(importFactor * float64(runtime.GOMAXPROCS(0)))),
		BackgroundWorkers: repo.GetScheduler().Workers, AsyncIndexing: async, Pid: os.Getpid(),
	}
	// mu is held by whoever changes the result or writes it: the test, and
	// what samples the progress.
	var mu sync.Mutex
	write := func() error {
		raw, err := json.MarshalIndent(result, "", "  ")
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return os.WriteFile(out, raw, 0o644)
	}
	update := func(change func()) {
		mu.Lock()
		defer mu.Unlock()
		change()
		require.NoError(t, write())
	}
	update(func() {})
	t.Logf("%s through a shard: %d of the %d rows of %s, %d dimensions, by %d callers in batches of %d | %d batch workers, "+
		"%d background workers, async indexing %t | config %+v", indexType, n, train.rows, datasetDir, train.dims, callers,
		batchSize, result.ImportWorkers, result.BackgroundWorkers, async, userConfig)

	// The rows in the order they go in: that of the other harnesses of the
	// index, which shuffle the rows that go in among themselves.
	order := make([]uint32, n)
	for i := range order {
		order[i] = uint32(i)
	}
	if shuffle {
		rand.New(rand.NewPCG(1, 1)).Shuffle(len(order), func(i, j int) { order[i], order[j] = order[j], order[i] })
	}

	// The readers read the rows of every batch ahead of the callers, so that
	// a caller does not wait for the dataset between two batch calls.
	type prepared struct {
		rows    []uint32
		vectors [][]float32
	}
	batches := make(chan prepared, 4*callers)
	stopReading := make(chan struct{})
	var stopReadingOnce sync.Once
	defer stopReadingOnce.Do(func() { close(stopReading) })
	var nextBatch, readNs atomic.Int64
	reading := enterrors.NewErrorGroupWrapper(logger)
	for range readers {
		reading.Go(func() error {
			var buf []byte
			for {
				select {
				case <-stopReading:
					return nil
				default:
				}
				from := (int(nextBatch.Add(1)) - 1) * batchSize
				if from >= n {
					return nil
				}
				rows := order[from:min(from+batchSize, n)]
				began := time.Now()
				vectors, kept, err := train.read(rows, buf)
				buf = kept
				readNs.Add(int64(time.Since(began)))
				if err != nil {
					stopReadingOnce.Do(func() { close(stopReading) })
					return err
				}
				select {
				case batches <- prepared{rows: rows, vectors: vectors}:
				case <-stopReading:
					return nil
				}
			}
		})
	}
	var readErr error
	readDone := make(chan struct{})
	enterrors.GoWrapper(func() {
		readErr = reading.Wait()
		close(batches)
		close(readDone)
	}, logger)
	// The first batches are read before the clock starts.
	prefilled := func() bool {
		select {
		case <-readDone:
			return true
		default:
			return len(batches) == cap(batches)
		}
	}
	for !prefilled() {
		time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
	}

	var inserted, foundNoBatch atomic.Int64
	startUsage, err := readShardE2ERusage()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	begin := time.Now()

	// The progress, every PE_PROGRESS seconds, until the run is flushed.
	sample := func() {
		s := shardE2ESample{Seconds: time.Since(begin).Seconds(), Inserted: inserted.Load()}
		if queues != nil {
			s.Pending = queues.pending()
		}
		mu.Lock()
		defer mu.Unlock()
		var last shardE2ESample
		if len(result.Progress) > 0 {
			last = result.Progress[len(result.Progress)-1]
		}
		s.PerSecond = float64(s.Inserted-last.Inserted) / (s.Seconds - last.Seconds)
		result.Progress = append(result.Progress, s)
		result.Inserted = s.Inserted
		if err := write(); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("write %s: %v", out, err)
		}
		t.Logf("%.0f s: %d of %d in (%.1f %%), %.0f a second since the last sample | waiting in the background queues: %v",
			s.Seconds, s.Inserted, n, 100*float64(s.Inserted)/float64(n), s.PerSecond, s.Pending)
	}
	stopSampling, sampled := make(chan struct{}), make(chan struct{})
	var stopSamplingOnce sync.Once
	enterrors.GoWrapper(func() {
		defer close(sampled)
		ticker := time.NewTicker(every)
		defer ticker.Stop()
		for {
			select {
			case <-stopSampling:
				return
			case <-ticker.C:
				sample()
			}
		}
	}, logger)
	stopSampler := func() {
		stopSamplingOnce.Do(func() { close(stopSampling) })
		<-sampled
	}
	defer stopSampler()

	inserting := enterrors.NewErrorGroupWrapper(logger)
	for range callers {
		inserting.Go(func() error {
			for {
				if len(batches) == 0 {
					foundNoBatch.Add(1)
				}
				next, ok := <-batches
				if !ok {
					return nil
				}
				batch := make(objects.BatchObjects, len(next.rows))
				for i, row := range next.rows {
					id := shardE2EUUID(row)
					batch[i] = objects.BatchObject{
						OriginalIndex: i,
						Object: &models.Object{
							Class:      shardE2EClass,
							ID:         id,
							Properties: map[string]interface{}{"row": int64(row)},
							Vector:     next.vectors[i],
						},
						UUID: id,
					}
				}
				res, err := repo.BatchPutObjects(ctx, batch, nil, 0)
				if err == nil {
					for _, object := range res {
						if object.Err != nil {
							err = errors.Wrapf(object.Err, "row %d", next.rows[object.OriginalIndex])
							break
						}
					}
				}
				if err != nil {
					stopReadingOnce.Do(func() { close(stopReading) })
					return err
				}
				inserted.Add(int64(len(batch)))
			}
		})
	}
	insertErr := inserting.Wait()
	lastBatch := time.Since(begin)
	require.NoError(t, insertErr)
	<-readDone
	require.NoError(t, readErr)
	require.Equal(t, int64(n), inserted.Load(), "the objects whose batch call returned")

	// point is the run at a clock that has just been read.
	point := func(took time.Duration) *shardE2EPoint {
		usage, err := readShardE2ERusage()
		require.NoError(t, err)
		return &shardE2EPoint{
			Seconds: took.Seconds(), ObjectsPerSecond: float64(n) / took.Seconds(), Usage: usage.since(startUsage),
		}
	}
	atLastBatch := point(lastBatch)
	var pendingAtLastBatch map[string]int64
	if queues != nil {
		pendingAtLastBatch = queues.pending()
	}
	// Written at once, a small file: a run that stops in what follows has
	// left its first clock.
	update(func() {
		result.Inserted, result.LastBatch, result.PendingAtLastBatch = inserted.Load(), atLastBatch, pendingAtLastBatch
	})
	t.Logf("the last batch call returned at %.1f s: %.0f objects a second, %.0f s of CPU | waiting in the background "+
		"queues: %v", atLastBatch.Seconds, atLastBatch.ObjectsPerSecond, atLastBatch.Usage.CPUSeconds, pendingAtLastBatch)

	// The vector index with no background work left. With async indexing the
	// queue of the shard goes first: what it holds has not reached the index.
	if async {
		require.NoError(t, vq.Flush())
		for vq.Size() > 0 {
			time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
		}
		require.NoError(t, vq.Wait(ctx))
	}
	switch {
	case pe != nil:
		// Whatever maintenance is due, with the rule of an index at rest, and
		// then what the index wrote handed to the system.
		require.NoError(t, pe.Settle(ctx))
		require.NoError(t, pe.Flush())
	case hf != nil:
		require.NoError(t, queues.wait(ctx))
		require.NoError(t, hf.Flush())
	}
	backgroundDone := time.Since(begin)
	atBackgroundDone := point(backgroundDone)
	update(func() { result.BackgroundDone = atBackgroundDone })
	// And everything flushed: every memtable of the shard, those of the
	// objects and those of the index, in a segment.
	require.NoError(t, shard.Store().FlushMemtables(ctx))
	flushed := time.Since(begin)
	atFlushed := point(flushed)
	stopSampler()

	// The heap and the disk, without what the harness held.
	order = nil
	runtime.GC()
	runtime.GC()
	var mem runtime.MemStats
	runtime.ReadMemStats(&mem)
	dirBytes, err := shardE2EDirBytes(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	update(func() {
		result.Flushed = atFlushed
		result.DatasetReadSeconds = time.Duration(readNs.Load()).Seconds()
		result.CallersFoundNoBatch = foundNoBatch.Load()
		result.HeapInuse, result.HeapAlloc, result.HeapSys, result.Sys = mem.HeapInuse, mem.HeapAlloc, mem.HeapSys, mem.Sys
		result.DirBytes = dirBytes
	})
	t.Logf("no background work left at %.1f s, flushed at %.1f s: %.0f objects a second, %.0f s of CPU, %.1f GB written "+
		"to disk | heap in use %.1f MB, footprint %.1f MB, %.2f GB on disk | the readers took %.1f s of the dataset, a "+
		"caller found no batch %d times", atBackgroundDone.Seconds, atFlushed.Seconds, atFlushed.ObjectsPerSecond,
		atFlushed.Usage.CPUSeconds, float64(atFlushed.Usage.BytesWritten)/1e9, float64(mem.HeapInuse)/1e6,
		float64(atFlushed.Usage.Footprint)/1e6, float64(dirBytes)/1e9, result.DatasetReadSeconds,
		result.CallersFoundNoBatch)

	// The queries, one at a time, through the search of the database, which
	// is the search of the shard and the objects of its results.
	if queryLimit > 0 {
		queries, truth, err := shardE2EReadQueries(datasetDir, shapes, train.dims, queryLimit, k)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		latencies := make([]float64, len(queries))
		hits := 0
		for q, query := range queries {
			started := time.Now()
			res, err := repo.VectorSearch(ctx, dto.GetParams{
				ClassName:  shardE2EClass,
				Pagination: &filters.Pagination{Limit: k},
			}, []string{""}, []models.Vector{query})
			latencies[q] = float64(time.Since(started).Nanoseconds()) / 1e6
			require.NoError(t, err, "query %d", q)
			got := make([]uint32, 0, len(res))
			for _, r := range res {
				row, err := shardE2ERow(r.ID)
				require.NoError(t, err, "query %d returned the id %q", q, r.ID)
				got = append(got, row)
			}
			for _, want := range truth[q] {
				if slices.Contains(got, want) {
					hits++
				}
			}
		}
		search := &shardE2ESearch{Queries: len(queries), K: k}
		var total float64
		for _, ms := range latencies {
			total += ms
		}
		sorted := slices.Clone(latencies)
		slices.Sort(sorted)
		at := func(q float64) float64 {
			return sorted[max(0, min(len(sorted)-1, int(math.Ceil(q*float64(len(sorted))))-1))]
		}
		search.MeanMs, search.QPS = total/float64(len(queries)), 1e3*float64(len(queries))/total
		search.P50Ms, search.P95Ms, search.P99Ms, search.MaxMs = at(0.50), at(0.95), at(0.99), sorted[len(sorted)-1]
		if n == train.rows {
			recall := float64(hits) / float64(len(queries)*k)
			search.Recall = &recall
			t.Logf("%d queries, one at a time: recall@%d %.4f | %.2f ms a query, p50 %.2f, p99 %.2f", len(queries), k, recall,
				search.MeanMs, search.P50Ms, search.P99Ms)
		} else {
			t.Logf("%d queries, one at a time: %.2f ms a query, p50 %.2f, p99 %.2f | no recall: the neighbors of the dataset "+
				"are over its %d rows, and %d went in", len(queries), search.MeanMs, search.P50Ms, search.P99Ms, train.rows, n)
		}
		var pendingAfterSearch map[string]int64
		if queues != nil {
			// A search of HFresh enqueues a merge for every posting it finds
			// too small.
			pendingAfterSearch = queues.pending()
			require.NoError(t, queues.wait(ctx))
		}
		update(func() { result.Search, result.PendingAfterSearch = search, pendingAfterSearch })
	}

	shutting := time.Now()
	closed = true
	require.NoError(t, repo.Shutdown(context.Background()))
	shutdown := time.Since(shutting)
	dirBytesAtEnd, err := shardE2EDirBytes(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	update(func() {
		result.ShutdownSeconds, result.DirBytesAtEnd, result.Done = shutdown.Seconds(), dirBytesAtEnd, true
	})
	t.Logf("shut in %.1f s, %.2f GB on disk", shutdown.Seconds(), float64(dirBytesAtEnd)/1e9)
}
